variants: DC: Direct compression (dispense > sift > blend > lubricate > compress > [coat] > pack)
WG-HS: Wet granulation, high-shear mixer granulator (RMG) + fluid-bed or tray drying + dry milling
WG-FB: Fluid-bed (top-spray) granulation, where granulation and drying happen in one unit
DG-RC: Dry granulation by roller compaction (slugging is a legacy alternative)
FC: Film coating, aqueous or organic, non-functional (typical weight gain 2-4%, often 3%)
FC-F: Functional film coating (enteric or gastro-resistant, modified-release); weight gain is linked to a CQA
SC: Sugar coating (seal coat, sub-coat, smoothing, colour, polish)
UNC: Uncoated tablets (including scored, chewable, dispersible, orodispersible and effervescent sub-types, which differ in disintegration and RH limits)
CM: Continuous manufacturing (continuous direct compression or continuous granulation) per ICH Q13; batch is defined by input quantity, output quantity or run time at a defined mass flow rate
PK-BL: Blister packing, thermoform PVC or PVC/PVDC (or Aclar) with printed Al lidding foil, or cold-form Alu-Alu
PK-ST: Strip packing (Al/Al or paper/poly/foil strips)
PK-BT: HDPE bottles with counting, desiccant (canister or sachet), optional cotton/rayon coil, CRC or plain cap, induction-seal liner, pressure-sensitive label
PK-SEC: Secondary packaging: leaflet (PIL) + carton, overprinting (batch, mfg date, expiry, price/MRP), anti-tampering device (EU)
PK-SER: Serialization and aggregation (EU FMD unique identifier; US DSCSA product identifier; India Schedule H2 QR code; other markets)
PK-TER: Tertiary packaging: shipper/case with labels (GS1-128/SSCC), palletization
POT: Potent, hormonal or cytotoxic product mode (containment, dedicated parts, HBEL-based cleaning); cross-cuts all process variants
HYG: Hygroscopic, moisture-sensitive or effervescent mode (tight RH limits, exposure-time limits, desiccant packaging); cross-cuts all process variants

unit_operations.name: Batch record issuance and batch initiation
unit_operations.purpose: Issue a controlled, accurate reproduction of the approved master record for one batch, assign a unique batch number and fix the batch's regulatory identity. Basis: 21 CFR 211.188(a) (reproduction of the master record, checked for accuracy, dated, signed) and EU GMP Ch.4 4.20 (batch record based on the approved formula and instructions, prepared so as to avoid transcription errors). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-211/subpart-J/section-211.188 ; https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/104b3eb8-81a7-4858-9419-cb06562adb66_en?filename=chapter4_01-2011_en.pdf
bmr_records: Product name, product code, dosage form, strength, market/country variant, marketing authorisation / NDA / ANDA / manufacturing licence number
Master Production Record (MFR/MBR) document ID, version and effective date; eBR recipe ID and version; statement 'accurate reproduction checked for accuracy, dated, signed'
Batch number (unique, per numbering SOP, system-generated and checked for uniqueness across all sites) and ERP process-order number
Batch size: theoretical blend mass (kg), theoretical number of tablets, theoretical core tablet weight (mg), theoretical coated tablet weight (mg)
Manufacturing site, building, suite/room, line or equipment train
Issued by (QA) and received by (Production), each with date/time; page count or section list for hybrid/paper records
Manufacturing (production) date definition and calculated expiry date; storage statement
Batch purpose flag (commercial, PPQ/validation, exhibit, continued process verification), plus referenced planned deviations and change controls
Product hazard flags: potent/cytotoxic (OEB or HBEL class), hygroscopic, light-sensitive, controlled substance, organic solvent use
critical_process_parameters: Not applicable (administrative step), but it fixes the parameters every later step inherits: the MBR version, which carries the CPP ranges, IPC limits and yield limits

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Only the current approved and effective MBR/recipe can be issued; superseded or draft versions are blocked (21 CFR 211.186, 211.188(a))
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Block issuance. If a wrong version was already issued or executed: deviation, QA impact assessment, batch placed on hold

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: No duplicate within the product/site/company namespace
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Block. Reissue under a new number with a documented reason

signatures_required: Master recipe approval (before effective): author, Production head and QA head (21 CFR 211.186(a) requires full signature of one person and independent check/signature by a second person)
special_checks: Readiness pre-check: required materials are QC-released and within retest/expiry; equipment in the train is qualified, within calibration and not under maintenance
Warn if the MBR version differs from the registered process (regulatory variant mismatch)
Controlled-substance batches: quota/permit check where applicable (jurisdiction-specific; not verified here)
time_limits_or_hold_times: EU start of shelf life: expiry is counted from the batch release date, provided release is no more than 30 days after the production date; otherwise from the production date. Production date = first step in which the active ingredient is combined with other ingredients (CPMP/QWP/072/96). https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/scientific-guideline/note-guidance-start-shelf-life-finished-dosage-form-annex-note-guidance-manufacture-finished-dosage-form_en.pdf

US: expiry must be supported by stability data (21 CFR 211.137). Date of manufacture is commonly defined in the firm's SOP as the date the API is first mixed with other materials. That definition comes from secondary sources and is NOT verified in an FDA text

unit_operations.name: Pre-operation checks: line clearance, equipment cleaning status, environmental conditions (repeated before EVERY unit operation and room/equipment change)
unit_operations.purpose: Confirm the room and equipment are free of the previous product, materials and documents, are clean, within clean hold time, qualified, calibrated and correctly labelled, and that the environment is within limits. Basis: EU 4.20 (pre-processing check that equipment and work station are clear and clean); 21 CFR 211.67 (cleaning); 211.182 (equipment cleaning and use log); 211.42/211.46 (facilities, T/RH). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-211/subpart-J/section-211.182
bmr_records: Room/area ID; previous product name and batch number in the room and on each piece of equipment
Equipment ID(s); qualification status; calibration due date (balances, temperature/RH sensors, pressure gauges, tachometers)
Cleaning status label reference: type of cleaning (batch-to-batch / product changeover / major), cleaned by, checked by, date/time of cleaning completion
Clean equipment hold time: elapsed time since cleaning vs validated maximum
Line clearance checklist items (floors, drains, under/inside machines, hoppers, sieves, dust collectors, bins, scoops, printed documents/labels), each marked OK/NA
Environmental readings at start: room temperature (°C), RH (%), differential pressure (Pa) vs product-specific limits; EMS reference
'Under process' status label applied (product, batch, stage, date)
Equipment use-log entry auto-created: date, time, product, batch number, operation (211.182)
critical_process_parameters: Room temperature and RH (product-specific). Typical OSD values: 20-25 °C and RH NMT 55-60%. Hygroscopic products often NMT 35-40% RH; effervescent often NMT 20-25% RH. Typical industry values, NOT regulatory (unverified)
Differential pressure cascade and airlock integrity; dust extraction running for dust-generating steps

in_process_controls.frequency: At start of each step; then continuous EMS or manual every 2-4 h (typical)
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Product-specific limits in the MBR (EU GMP Ch.3: temperature, humidity and ventilation must not adversely affect products; 21 CFR 211.46)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Hygroscopic/effervescent product: stop exposure, close containers, raise a deviation, QA impact assessment (e.g., LOD retest). Other products: evaluate against the excursion SOP

in_process_controls.frequency: Before each operation and after any product/batch change
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: No residue from the previous product, no foreign materials, no documents/labels from the previous batch
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Do not start. Re-clean or remove items and repeat line clearance. If previous-product residue is found after QA verification: deviation

special_checks: eBR interlock: the step cannot start if clean hold time has expired, the equipment is due for calibration or preventive maintenance, the previous line clearance is not approved, or the status is 'To be cleaned'

Dedicated product-contact parts (e.g., FBD filter bags) for potent/sensitising products (Schedule M Part I-B text, secondary source https://pharmastate.academy/manufacture-of-oral-solid-dosage-forms-tablets-and-capsules/)

Cross-contamination control per EU GMP Ch.5 5.17-5.22 (technical and organisational measures) and Ch.3 3.6 (dedicated facilities when risk cannot be controlled or HBEL does not support it). https://www.gmp-compliance.org/gmp-news/cross-contamination-topic-of-the-revisions-of-chapters-3-and-5-eu-gmp-guideline
time_limits_or_hold_times: Clean equipment hold time (CEHT): validated per equipment/product group; commonly 72 h up to 7 days (industry, unverified). Exceeded means re-clean

Dirty equipment hold time (DEHT): the time from end of use to start of cleaning; commonly 24-72 h (industry, unverified). Exceeded means deviation and possibly an enhanced cleaning cycle. Regulators expect both CEHT and DEHT to be established and monitored (https://www.pharmtech.com/view/equipment-hold-time-cleaning-validation; WHO TRS 1033 Annex 2 https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/annex-2-trs-1033)
unit_operations.variant_applicability: All variants; repeated for every room and equipment used, and for packaging lines (see packaging line clearance)

unit_operations.name: Dispensing / weighing of raw materials (including potency, assay and LOD/water adjustment and overage)
unit_operations.purpose: Weigh the exact quantity of each QC-released component per the bill of materials, corrected for actual API potency and moisture, with independent verification. Basis: 21 CFR 211.101(b)-(d); 211.188(b)(3)-(4); EU GMP Ch.5 dispensing clause ('each dispensed material and its weight or volume should be independently checked and the check recorded', cited as 5.33 in the pre-2015 numbering; current number not verified). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-211/subpart-F/section-211.101
bmr_records: Material code, name, grade (e.g., Ph.Eur./USP/IP) and function (API, diluent, binder, disintegrant, glidant, lubricant, colour)
Manufacturer and supplier; internal lot (GRN) number; QC analytical reference (AR) number; release status; retest or expiry date
Standard quantity per batch (from the MBR) and allowed range
API assay (reported basis: as-is, anhydrous or dried), water content (KF %) or LOD %, salt/base conversion factor, calculated potency factor, and the resulting potency-adjusted quantity
Compensating excipient (e.g., MCC or lactose) standard quantity, adjustment and adjusted quantity
Overage % (only if registered) and the resulting quantity
Per container: container number, gross, tare and net weight; number of containers dispensed
Balance ID, capacity, readability, minimum weight, daily verification reference and result; weighing booth/RLAF ID and air velocity/ΔP check
Actual quantity dispensed, and deviation from target in %
Dispensing date and start/end time; sequence number of material in booth
Dispensed-material label (product, batch, material, lot/AR, gross/tare/net, dispensed by/checked by, date)
Remnant quantities returned to stores and container status updated (partial-container reconciliation)
Material transfer: issued by (warehouse) and received by (production)
critical_process_parameters: Accuracy of the net weight within the dispensing tolerance defined in the MBR (commonly ±0.5% for API and ±1% for excipients in industry practice; unverified; must be product-specific)

Balance suitability: net weight ≥ balance minimum weight. USP <41> criteria for 'accurately weighed' analytical use: repeatability 2×SD/nominal ≤ 0.10%, accuracy within 0.10% (test weight between 5% and 100% of capacity). These are applied to production balances by extension via USP <1251> and SOP; that extension is not an explicit production requirement (https://www.usp.org/frequently-asked-questions/balances-and-weighing-analytical-balance)
Correct potency calculation; use of the correct CoA values

in_process_controls.frequency: Before first use each day/shift (and per calibration SOP)
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Within the SOP tolerance at the check weights; within the calibration period
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Balance tagged out of use; impact assessment of weighings since the last good check; deviation

in_process_controls.test: Material identity/status verification (barcode scan of container label vs BOM, lot released, within retest date)
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Material code, lot and status match the BOM; FEFO respected (21 CFR 211.101(b), 211.84, 211.87)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Hard block. Wrong material presented: deviation
Hard block until corrected by adding or removing material; never record out-of-tolerance weight as final

in_process_controls.test: Independent verification of weight, identity and container labelling
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Second person verifies, or automated equipment under 211.68 plus one verifying person (21 CFR 211.101(c),(d))
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Step cannot be completed without verification

signatures_required: Checked by: second person (warehouse/production officer), or system-verified + one person when the weighing system is validated under 211.68
Calculation of the potency adjustment: performed by one person, independently verified by a second (by analogy to 211.103; typical SOP practice)
special_checks: Potency adjustment only with approved CoA values of the specific lot; multiple API lots must be pro-rated lot by lot
Compensation must keep the formula within the registered composition. Overages must be in the MA and justified per ICH Q8(R2) pharmaceutical development
Dispense APIs in a separate booth/time slot from excipients or with cleaning between; one material at a time in the booth
Potent/cytotoxic: containment (isolator/downflow booth with validated containment), closed transfer, PPE (PAPR), wipe-down of container exterior, restricted access, dedicated scoops
Light-sensitive: yellow/sodium light
Hygroscopic: RH limit and maximum exposure time; containers closed immediately
time_limits_or_hold_times: Dispensed-material hold time before use (validated; often 7-30 days in closed double LDPE bags; industry, unverified). Scope per WHO TRS 992 Annex 4 hold-time guidance https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/trs992-annex4

unit_operations.name: Sifting / screening / de-lumping
unit_operations.purpose: Remove lumps and foreign matter and de-agglomerate before mixing. Revised Schedule M Part I-B: all ingredients for a dry product shall be sifted before use unless the quality of the input material can be assured (text as quoted by secondary source https://pharmastate.academy/manufacture-of-oral-solid-dosage-forms-tablets-and-capsules/)
bmr_records: Sifter / co-mil / cone-mill ID; screen mesh number or aperture (µm) per material as specified in the MBR
Screen integrity check before and after use (intact / not intact), with verifier
Material, lot and quantity fed; quantity recovered; oversize retained and its handling (de-lumped and passed / rejected)
Foreign matter observed (Y/N, description)
Magnet/grate check (if fitted)
Dust extraction ON; start and end time
Stage yield (output/input %)
critical_process_parameters: Screen aperture (e.g., #20/#30/#40/#60 per the MBR; lubricants typically finer, e.g., #60)
Sifter vibration or mill impeller speed

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: No tears, holes or loose mesh
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Post-use damage: quarantine all material sifted since the last intact check, re-sift through an intact screen, look for screen fragments (metal detector/visual), deviation
Deviation. Hold material; QA and warehouse investigate the supplier lot

signatures_required: Screen integrity verified by: supervisor or IPQA
special_checks: Dust control; sift API in a contained way for potent products
time_limits_or_hold_times: Same as dispensed materials unless separately validated

unit_operations.name: Dry mixing / pre-blending (including geometric dilution for low-dose API)
unit_operations.purpose: Homogeneously distribute API and intragranular excipients before granulation, or before final blend in direct compression
bmr_records: Equipment ID (RMG/blender) and working capacity; occupancy % of the blender
Order of addition (checkbox per material, in MBR sequence)
Impeller and chopper speed (slow/fast, rpm) and mixing time, OR blender rpm and time/number of revolutions
Ammeter/power/torque reading (RMG)
Geometric dilution steps (low-dose API): quantities per step
Start and end time
critical_process_parameters: Fill level (blenders commonly 30-70% occupancy; industry, unverified)

in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Out of range: deviation; BU or pre-blend testing may be required by QA

special_checks: Low-dose products: validated pre-blend/trituration procedure, possibly pre-blend uniformity testing
time_limits_or_hold_times: Normally proceed immediately to the next step; any hold must be within a validated time
unit_operations.variant_applicability: WG-HS, WG-FB, DG-RC (pre-blend before compaction), DC (first blending stage)

unit_operations.name: Binder solution / dispersion preparation
unit_operations.purpose: Prepare the granulating fluid (e.g., PVP K30, HPMC, starch paste, gelatin) at the specified concentration
bmr_records: Vessel and stirrer IDs
Solvent: purified water (system/point of use ID and water release status) or organic solvent (IPA/ethanol: flameproof area, solvent lot)
Binder material, lot and quantity; solvent quantity
Water/paste temperature (e.g., starch paste made at an elevated temperature per the MBR); stirrer speed and time
Appearance (clear, lump-free, uniform); final weight; viscosity if specified
Preparation completion time and 'use before' time
critical_process_parameters: Total quantity of binder solution available for addition

in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Continue stirring or reprepare; deviation if reprepared
Expired: discard and reprepare; deviation

special_checks: Microbial risk for aqueous starch/gelatin pastes
Solvent safety (ATEX), and solvent quantity reconciliation
time_limits_or_hold_times: WHO TRS 992 Annex 4 lists binder preparation → granulation as a hold-time stage. Binder and coating solutions are generally used within the day / next shift (search-result summary of https://www.who.int/docs/default-source/medicines/norms-and-standards/guidelines/distribution/trs992-annex4.pdf)

unit_operations.name: Wet granulation - high-shear mixer granulator (RMG), including wet milling
unit_operations.purpose: Agglomerate the powder with binder to improve flow, density and content uniformity
bmr_records: RMG ID and bowl capacity
Dry-mix impeller/chopper speed and time
Binder addition: mode (pour/pump/spray), pump ID, addition rate (kg/min), start/end time, quantity added
Additional granulating fluid added (only if the MBR allows a range): quantity and justification
Wet massing: impeller and chopper speed (slow/fast) and time
Endpoint: amperage/power (kW)/torque value at endpoint; product temperature
Wet milling: mill ID, screen size, speed
Wet mass discharge time; wet weight (optional)
Transfer to dryer: time

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Within the validated endpoint range in the MBR
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Below range: extra fluid/massing only within MBR-permitted limits. Over-granulation or beyond the permitted extra fluid: deviation, QA assessment; possible impact on dissolution/hardness
As above

signatures_required: Extra fluid addition authorised by: production head/QA (if permitted)
special_checks: Capture PLC/SCADA data (trend) with audit trail; alarms reviewed in batch review
time_limits_or_hold_times: Wet granules → drying: typically immediate or within a short validated time (WHO TRS 992 Annex 4 lists wet granulation → drying as a hold stage)

unit_operations.name: Fluid-bed (top-spray) granulation
unit_operations.purpose: Granulate by spraying binder onto a fluidised powder bed, followed by in-situ drying
bmr_records: FBP/FBG ID; filter bag ID and integrity check (pre/post); bag dedication status for potent products
Inlet air temperature (set/actual), product bed temperature, exhaust temperature, air volume/flap %
Spray rate (g/min), atomisation air pressure (bar), nozzle size and position, peristaltic pump ID
Binder quantity sprayed; spray start/end time
Filter shaking interval/mode
Drying phase data and LOD results (see drying)
critical_process_parameters: Inlet air temperature and air volume

in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Adjust within range; excursion: deviation
Continue drying

special_checks: Filter bags: Schedule M Part I-B text says FBD filter bags shall not be used for different products without washing in between, and for certain highly potent or sensitising products bags specific to one product only shall be used (secondary-source wording; verify against the official notification)
time_limits_or_hold_times: As for granules/dried granules

unit_operations.name: Drying (fluid-bed dryer or tray dryer) with LOD endpoint
unit_operations.purpose: Remove granulating fluid to a validated moisture range, which affects compressibility, hardness, dissolution and stability
bmr_records: Dryer ID; filter bag ID and integrity (FBD); tray count and loading (tray dryer)
Inlet air temperature set/actual, product temperature, exhaust temperature, air flow; drying time; raking/intermittent air-dry cycles
LOD results: time of sampling, moisture analyser ID, method (e.g., halogen/IR at a set temperature and endpoint criterion, or oven per USP <731>), result %
Final LOD %; dried granule weight (gross/tare/net), container IDs
Stage yield (dried granules vs theoretical dry solids)
critical_process_parameters: Inlet air temperature, product temperature (max limit for heat-labile APIs), air volume

in_process_controls.frequency: Periodically near the end (e.g., every 10-15 min once product temperature plateaus) and at the endpoint; composite of several locations
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Product-specific range in the MBR, e.g., 1.5-3.0% w/w (illustrative; https://pharmagmpguide.com/high-lod-after-fbd/ is a secondary source). Surrogates (e.g., outlet temperature) are acceptable if justified: FDA draft 211.110 guidance, Jan 2025 https://www.fda.gov/media/184825/download
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Above upper limit: continue drying and retest. Below lower limit (over-dried): deviation; QA decides (re-humidification only if validated/approved)
Deviation; assess product loss and contamination

special_checks: Organic solvent granulation: residual solvent (ICH Q3C) may be controlled by LOD or GC per spec
time_limits_or_hold_times: Dried granules → lubrication/blending hold time (validated; WHO TRS 992 Annex 4 lists dried granules → lubrication/blending)

unit_operations.name: Dry granulation - roller compaction (including in-line milling)
unit_operations.purpose: Densify moisture/heat-sensitive formulations into ribbons and mill them into granules
bmr_records: Roller compactor ID; roll type (smooth/knurled/fluted)
Roll pressure/force (bar or kN/cm), roll gap (mm), roll speed (rpm), feed screw speed(s) (horizontal/vertical), deaeration vacuum
Ribbon appearance; ribbon thickness/solid fraction/density results
Mill type, screen aperture, mill speed, rotor direction
Fines recycled (only if MBR-permitted): quantity/%
Start/end time; granule weight and fines weight; stage yield
critical_process_parameters: Roll pressure (most critical), roll gap, feed-screw-to-roll speed ratio, mill screen size and speed (https://aiche.confex.com/aiche/s06/techprogram/P38067.HTM; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0378517320307547 - literature, not regulatory)

in_process_controls.frequency: At start-up and every 30-60 min (typical, unverified)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Adjust within validated ranges; segregate material made during the excursion; deviation

in_process_controls.test: Granule PSD (sieve analysis, USP <786>) and bulk/tapped density (USP <616>)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: QA assessment

special_checks: Recycling of fines must be in the validated process and registered; record recycled quantity for yield
time_limits_or_hold_times: Granules → blending hold time (validated)

unit_operations.name: Dry milling / sizing of granules
unit_operations.purpose: Reduce dried granules/ribbons to the target size distribution
bmr_records: Mill ID (co-mil, multimill, oscillating granulator, Fitzmill); screen aperture and type; screen integrity pre/post
Blade/impeller orientation (knife/impact), speed (rpm), feed rate
Input weight, output weight, oversize handling, stage yield
Start/end time

in_process_controls.action_on_failure: Quarantine, re-screen, deviation
QA assessment

special_checks: Metal fragments from mill: check screen/blade condition
time_limits_or_hold_times: Sized granules hold (validated)

unit_operations.name: Final blending and lubrication (including blend uniformity)
unit_operations.purpose: Mix granules with extragranular excipients, then lubricate; demonstrate adequacy of mixing (21 CFR 211.110(a)(3) 'adequacy of mixing to assure uniformity and homogeneity'). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-211/subpart-F/section-211.110
bmr_records: Blender ID (bin/IBC, octagonal, V, double-cone), working capacity, occupancy %
Actual granule weight; extragranular quantities (standard or proportionally adjusted per MBR formula, with the calculation shown and independently verified)
Pre-lubrication blending: rpm and time/number of revolutions
Lubricant (e.g., magnesium stearate) sifted through the specified mesh, quantity; lubrication rpm and time/revolutions
Blend uniformity sampling: sampling map/locations, thief type/ID, sample size (1-3× unit dose weight), number of samples, sample IDs sent to QC, AR number
BU results: individual % label claim, mean, SD, RSD%, min/max; pass/fail
Blend physical tests if specified: LOD, bulk/tapped density, Carr's index/Hausner ratio, PSD
Final blend weight: container/IBC IDs, gross/tare/net; stage yield
Blend label (product, batch, stage 'lubricated blend', net weight, date)
critical_process_parameters: Lubrication time (over-lubrication reduces hardness and slows dissolution)

in_process_controls.frequency: Per validated sampling plan (PPQ: enhanced, e.g., at least 10 locations × 3 replicates; routine: per control strategy, which may use stratified in-process dosage-unit testing or PAT/NIR)
in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Product-specific. Historic criteria from the FDA 2003 draft (withdrawn 7 Aug 2013): BU mean 90.0-110.0% and RSD ≤ 5.0%; stratified dosage-unit 'readily pass' RSD ≤ 4.0% with each location mean 90.0-110.0%. Current practice uses ASTM E2709/E2810 and ISPE BUCU recommendations (https://academy.gmp-compliance.org/guidemgr/files/5831DFT.PDF ; https://ispe.org/initiatives/blend-uniformity-content-uniformity/publications). FDA Q&A: sample size 1-3× dosage unit, larger with justification; 211.110 requires demonstrating adequacy of mixing but not necessarily direct blend testing (https://www.fda.gov/drugs/guidances-drugs/questions-and-answers-current-good-manufacturing-practice-regulations-production-and-process)
in_process_controls.action_on_failure: No automatic re-blending. OOS/deviation investigation (sampling error vs true non-uniformity) per 211.192. Re-blending is a reprocessing step: only per written procedure with QA approval (211.115); enhanced CU testing of the resulting tablets
QA assessment

signatures_required: Extragranular calculation: performed by and independently verified by
special_checks: Proportional adjustment of extragranular excipients only if the MBR explicitly allows it and the result stays within the registered formula
Sampling-thief technique and locations must match the validated map; record deviations from the map
Closed IBC transfer for potent products to limit segregation and exposure
time_limits_or_hold_times: Lubricated blend → compression hold time (validated; WHO TRS 992 Annex 4). Hold-time studies may include segregation/BU re-check

unit_operations.name: Compression (including de-dusting and metal detection)
unit_operations.purpose: Compress the lubricated blend into cores/tablets meeting weight, hardness, thickness, friability and disintegration targets
bmr_records: Tablet press ID, number of stations, single/double-sided

Tooling: punch and die set ID, shape, dimensions, embossing/debossing/score, number of punch sets installed, pre-use and post-use inspection results, tooling log reference, cumulative compression count
Set-up parameters: fill depth, pre-compression force (kN), main compression force (kN), turret speed (rpm)/output (tablets/h), feeder/paddle speed, ejection force (monitor)
Automatic weight control settings and reject limits (if fitted)
Set-up approval: first tablets checked and approved by IPQA (time); set-up reject quantity (kg)
De-duster ID; metal detector ID and challenge test results (test pieces Fe/non-Fe/SS with sizes) with time
IPC results table (see IPCs), time-stamped, with tester IDs (balance, thickness gauge, hardness tester, friabilator, DT apparatus)
Rejects: set-up rejects, weight-control rejects, metal-detector rejects, dust/fines, IPC samples destroyed (all by weight)
Output: container numbers, gross/tare/net per container; total good tablets (kg) and calculated number of tablets
Machine stoppages: time, duration, reason
QC samples (composite from start/middle/end) with AR number; stage yield

in_process_controls.typical_limit_or_reference: Target ± in-house limit (e.g., ±2-3%) within the pharmacopoeial limits

Impact on shelf life (EU: evaluate effect on shelf life)

yield_and_reconciliation_rules: The master record must state the theoretical weight or measure at appropriate phases and the theoretical yield, including the maximum and minimum % beyond which a 211.192 investigation is required (21 CFR 211.186(b)(6)-(7)). The software must refuse to make an MBR effective without limits for each yield-bearing stage. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-211/subpart-J/section-211.186

Actual yield and % of theoretical must be determined at the conclusion of each appropriate phase (211.103). The calculation is performed by one person and independently verified by a second, or calculated by automated equipment under 211.68 and verified by one person.

EU: the MBR states the expected final yield with acceptable limits and relevant intermediate yields (EU 4.17). Any significant deviation from expected yield is recorded and investigated (EU GMP Ch.5, stated as 5.41 in search results).

Yield outside limits, or ANY unexplained discrepancy, is investigated per 211.192 whether or not the batch has been distributed, and the investigation extends to other batches of the same and other products that may be associated (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-211/subpart-J/section-211.192).

A yield above 100% (e.g., >100.5%) is also a discrepancy (weighing error, incorrect count conversion, moisture pick-up, material from another batch) and must trigger the same investigation. Do not use a one-sided lower limit.

Stage yield limits are product-specific and derived from historical process data (process capability). Illustrative only, not regulatory: sifting ≥99.0%; granulation+drying (dry basis) ≥97.0%; milling ≥98.5%; blending/lubrication ≥98.5%; compression 97.0-100.5%; film coating (on a coated-weight basis) 97.5-100.5%; inspection ≥98.0%; overall manufacture ≥95.0%; packaging ≥97.0%. Flag as configurable.

Reconciliation (mass balance) differs from yield: all input must be accounted for as good output + samples + rejects + documented losses + returns. Unaccounted quantity beyond limits requires investigation even when yield passes.

Labelling reconciliation: issued = used + damaged/destroyed + returned + specimens/samples. Discrepancies between finished product quantity and labelling issued that fall outside narrow preset limits based on historical data must be evaluated and investigated per 211.192 (211.125(c)).

Waiver: labelling reconciliation is waived for cut or roll labelling only when a 100% examination for correct labelling is performed per 211.122(g)(2) (validated electronic/electromechanical verification). The software should require the validated vision system's challenge records before applying the waiver.

Excess labelling bearing lot/control numbers must be destroyed (211.125(e)). EU: unused batch-coded packaging materials destroyed and destruction recorded; un-coded printed materials returned to stock only per a documented procedure (EU Ch.5 packaging section).
Returned labelling must be maintained and stored so as to prevent mix-ups and provide proper identification (211.125(e)); returns require a count and warehouse receipt.

EU: any significant or unusual discrepancy found in reconciling bulk and printed packaging materials against units produced must be investigated and satisfactorily accounted for BEFORE release (EU Ch.5 packaging section; paragraph number differs between the pre-2015 (5.56) and current versions and is not verified).

EU 4.21(h): if robust electronic controls are in place during packaging, there may be justification for not including all reconciliation quantities in the batch packaging record. The system should support this only by QA-approved configuration.

Discrepancy handling workflow: (1) stop BPR closure and block release; (2) physical recount of returns and rejects; (3) search line, surrounding lines, waste bins and reject bins; (4) check machine counter validity and set-up waste records; (5) check for printed material found in other batches (mix-up risk) and extend to other batches packed on the same line/time window; (6) raise a deviation with root cause and CAPA; (7) QA decision (release, reject, recall assessment if distributed).
Serial-number reconciliation: commissioned = shipped (aggregated) + decommissioned (with reason codes: QC sample, destroyed, damaged, rejected) + retained. Mismatch blocks release/shipment.

Reprocessing requires written procedures and QCU approval (211.115). Reprocessed quantities enter the receiving batch's genealogy and yield calculation as separately identified inputs (EU 4.20(d) requires recording the batch number and amount of any recovered/reprocessed material added).

Rejected in-process material must be identified and controlled under a quarantine system to prevent use (211.110(d)). Rejected/discarded tablets from compression must be isolated in identified containers with quantity recorded (Schedule M Part I-B text, secondary source).

calculations.name: As-is assay (purity) of API
calculations.formula: Assay_asis(%) = Assay_anhydrous(%) × (100 − Water%) / 100  [or Assay_dried × (100 − LOD%) / 100 if assay is reported on the dried basis]
calculations.notes: Use the CoA values of the specific lot. Water by KF (USP <921>) or LOD (USP <731>) per the API monograph. Secondary sources: https://www.arlok.com/WaterContentofAPIs/ ; https://sgsystemsglobal.com/glossary/potency-adjustment-factor/

calculations.name: Potency-adjusted API quantity
calculations.formula: Q_API,actual = Q_API,std × 100 / Assay_asis(%)  ; with salt/base conversion: Q_API,std = Q_label(base) × (MW_salt / MW_base) × N_tablets ; with a registered overage: Q_API,std × (1 + Overage%/100)
calculations.notes: Example: water 4.5%, assay 99.8% anhydrous gives as-is 95.31% and factor 1.049. Q_std is the MBR quantity at 100% potency. Overage only if registered and justified (ICH Q8(R2)). Multiple lots: allocate per lot, each with its own factor.

calculations.name: Compensating excipient quantity
calculations.formula: Q_diluent,actual = Q_diluent,std − (Q_API,actual − Q_API,std)
calculations.notes: Keeps the total batch/core mass constant. The diluent (e.g., MCC/lactose) and any cap on adjustment must be defined in the MBR, and the result must stay within the registered composition. If the API is below 100% as-is, the diluent decreases; the system must block a negative or out-of-range result.

calculations.name: LOD/water adjustment for an excipient or intermediate specified on dry basis
calculations.formula: Q_actual = Q_dry,std × 100 / (100 − LOD%)
calculations.notes: Only if the MBR specifies a dry-basis quantity.

calculations.name: Theoretical batch mass by stage
calculations.formula: TY_stage(kg) = Σ (non-volatile solids charged up to that stage) − (planned samples removed, if the SOP deducts them) ; coated: TY_coated = mass of cores charged × (1 + WG_target%/100)  [or cores + theoretical coating solids applied]
calculations.notes: Granulating fluids (water/IPA) are volatile and excluded; residual moisture makes yields slightly higher, so the limits must reflect it.

calculations.name: Theoretical number of tablets per batch
calculations.formula: N_theo = (Theoretical blend mass in mg) / (Theoretical core tablet weight in mg) = (Batch kg × 10^6) / W_theo(mg)
calculations.notes: Example: 300 kg blend, 300 mg tablet gives 1,000,000 tablets. For coated products use cores; the coated count equals the core count consumed.

calculations.name: Actual number of tablets (count by weight)
calculations.formula: N_actual = Net weight of good tablets (mg) / Average tablet weight (mg)
calculations.notes: Average weight from a defined sample (e.g., 100 tablets) at the end of the run or from IPC averages. Record the method; for counter-based counts, record counter ID and validation.

calculations.name: Actual yield %
calculations.formula: Yield% = Actual output (kg or units) / Theoretical output (kg or units) × 100  (stage yield: output_stage / input_stage × 100 ; cumulative yield: output_stage / batch theoretical × 100)
calculations.notes: 211.103 requires independent verification. Compare against MBR min/max; outside limits triggers 211.192.

calculations.name: Reconciliation % (mass balance)
calculations.formula: Recon% = (Good output + IPC destructive samples + QC samples + retention/reserve samples + rejects + documented losses (e.g., dust collector, set-up waste) + returned material) / Total input × 100
calculations.notes: Must be within MBR limits; the unaccounted remainder = Input − Σ accounted.

calculations.name: Uniformity of mass limits (Ph.Eur. 2.9.5 / IP)
calculations.formula: p = 10% if W̄ ≤ 80 mg; 7.5% if 80 < W̄ < 250 mg; 5% if W̄ ≥ 250 mg. Individual limits = W̄ × (1 ± p/100); outer limits = W̄ × (1 ± 2p/100). Pass: NMT 2 of 20 outside ±p and 0 outside ±2p
calculations.notes: Applies to uncoated and film-coated tablets. https://www.drugfuture.com/Pharmacopoeia/EP7/DATA/20905E.PDF (EP7 copy; current text is harmonised and unchanged per search).

calculations.name: IPC average-weight and group-weight limits
calculations.formula: Avg-weight limits = W_target × (1 ± a/100) where a = in-house IPC tolerance (e.g., 2-3%); group weight of n tablets = n × W_target × (1 ± g/100)
calculations.notes: In-house tolerances must be tighter than release limits and derived from process capability (211.110(b): in-process specs derived from process averages and variability with suitable statistics).

calculations.name: USP <905> content uniformity acceptance value
calculations.notes: L1 = 15.0 and L2 = 25.0 confirmed by search of https://www.usp.org/sites/default/files/usp/document/harmonization/excipients/m99694.pdf (Stage 4 official 1 Aug 2023). The k values and M rules are from memory of the harmonised text: verify (T > 101.5 case omitted).

calculations.name: USP <905> weight variation estimated content
calculations.formula: x_i = w_i × A / W̄  (A = assay result in % label claim from a representative sample; w_i = individual weight; W̄ = mean weight); then compute AV as above
calculations.notes: Allowed for uncoated/film-coated tablets when API ≥ 25 mg and ≥ 25% of unit weight (Table 1; from memory, not fully verified).

calculations.name: Friability %
calculations.formula: F% = (W_initial − W_final) / W_initial × 100
calculations.notes: USP <1216>/Ph.Eur. 2.9.7: ~6.5 g sample (tablets ≤650 mg) or 10 tablets (>650 mg), 100 rotations at 25 ±1 rpm; NMT 1.0%; repeat twice more if doubtful and use the mean of three.

calculations.name: Tablet tensile strength (round, flat-faced)
calculations.formula: σ = 2F / (π · D · t)  (F = breaking force N, D = diameter, t = thickness)
calculations.notes: USP <1217> concept; normalises hardness across tooling. 1 kp = 9.807 N.

calculations.name: Coating weight gain %
calculations.formula: WG% = (W̄_coated − W̄_core) / W̄_core × 100 ; target coated weight = W̄_core × (1 + WG_target/100)
calculations.notes: Weigh the same number of tablets (e.g., 100) each time; correct for moisture if required.

calculations.name: Coating suspension required
calculations.formula: M_susp = (M_cores × WG_target/100) / (Solids%/100) × (1 + Loss%/100)
calculations.notes: Loss% = validated spray/process loss (e.g., 10-25%, product/equipment-specific). Record prepared vs sprayed quantities.

calculations.name: Blend uniformity statistics
calculations.formula: Mean = Σx_i/n ; SD = sqrt(Σ(x_i − mean)^2/(n − 1)) ; RSD% = SD/Mean × 100 ; location mean for stratified plans
calculations.notes: Acceptance per validated plan (ASTM E2709/E2810 or product-specific).

calculations.name: Dissolution acceptance (immediate release, USP <711>)
calculations.formula: S1: each of 6 ≥ Q+5%. S2: mean of 12 ≥ Q, none < Q−15%. S3: mean of 24 ≥ Q, NMT 2 < Q−15%, none < Q−25%
calculations.notes: https://www.uspnf.com/sites/default/files/usp_pdf/EN/USPNF/revisions/m99470-gc_711.pdf

calculations.name: Disintegration staged acceptance (USP <701>)
calculations.formula: 6 units all disintegrate → pass; if 1-2 fail → 12 more; pass if ≥16 of 18
calculations.notes: https://www.uspnf.com/sites/default/files/usp_pdf/EN/USPNF/generalChapter701.pdf

calculations.name: Blister theoretical quantities
calculations.formula: Blisters_theo = N_tablets_issued / tablets_per_blister ; Cartons_theo = Blisters_theo / blisters_per_carton ; Shippers_theo = Cartons_theo / cartons_per_shipper
calculations.notes: Used for material requirements and yield.

calculations.name: Blister (bulk tablet) reconciliation
calculations.formula: Recon% = [(Good blisters × tablets/blister) + tablets in rejected blisters + tablets in leak/IPC samples + QC/retention samples (tablets) + loose rejected tablets + bulk returned] / Tablets issued × 100
calculations.notes: Tablets issued are usually calculated by weight: net bulk weight / average tablet weight.

calculations.name: Printed foil / label / carton / leaflet reconciliation
calculations.formula: Recon% = (Used + Set-up waste + Damaged/rejected + Batch-coded destroyed + Un-coded returned + Specimens) / Issued × 100 ; Discrepancy = Issued − Σ ; foil used(m) = number of machine indexes × index pitch length (or by weight: Δkg / g per m)
calculations.notes: Units used = packs produced × components per pack. Count-by-weight: Count = Net weight / unit weight (average of 100). Discrepancy outside preset limits: investigation (211.125(c)).

calculations.name: Serial number reconciliation
calculations.formula: SN_commissioned = SN_aggregated/shipped + SN_decommissioned(by reason) + SN_samples/retained ; Unaccounted = SN_commissioned − Σ
calculations.notes: Must equal zero before release.

calculations.name: Hold-time compliance
calculations.formula: Elapsed = t_now − t_end(previous stage) ; compliant if Elapsed ≤ Max_hold(stage) ; CEHT elapsed = t_use_start − t_cleaning_end ; DEHT elapsed = t_cleaning_start − t_use_end
calculations.notes: 211.111; WHO TRS 992 Annex 4.

calculations.name: Expiry date (EU rule)
calculations.formula: If (Release date − Production date) ≤ 30 days: Expiry = Release date + shelf life; else Expiry = Production date + shelf life. Production date = first combination of API with other ingredients
calculations.notes: CPMP/QWP/072/96. Many companies print expiry as 'end of month', which is a market-specific rule.

calculations.name: Proportional extragranular adjustment (only if MBR allows)
calculations.formula: Q_extra,actual = Q_extra,std × (Actual dried granule weight / Theoretical dried granule weight)
calculations.notes: Common in some generics practice to keep lubricant/disintegrant ratios constant. It changes the theoretical tablet count, so the eBR must recalculate downstream theoretical yields and flag it for QA review.

edition_specific_features.feature: Recipe-driven dispensing with a potency/LOD/salt-factor calculator, multi-lot pro-rating, compensating-excipient logic and a registered-composition guardrail
edition_specific_features.why: Potency errors are a top source of assay failures. The calculation must be automatic, use CoA values pulled from LIMS, and be independently verified.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.101(c)-(d), 211.103, 211.186(b); EU GMP Ch.5 dispensing (independent check). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-211/subpart-F/section-211.101

edition_specific_features.feature: Scale/balance integration with minimum-weight enforcement, daily-check interlock, calibration-status interlock and barcode verification of material, lot and container
edition_specific_features.why: Removes transcription errors and makes automated verification (one-person check) permissible.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.68, 211.101(c)-(d); USP <41>/<1251> (https://www.usp.org/frequently-asked-questions/balances-and-weighing-analytical-balance)

edition_specific_features.feature: Hold-time engine: timers for clean/dirty equipment, dispensed materials, binder, wet mass, dried granules, lubricated blend, cores, coating suspension and coated bulk, with warnings and hard stops
edition_specific_features.why: Hold-time breaches are frequent inspection findings; the timing must be enforced by the system, not remembered by operators.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.111; WHO TRS 992 Annex 4 (https://www.who.int/publications/m/item/trs992-annex4); EMA finished dosage form guideline, 30-day rule (https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/documents/scientific-guideline/guideline-manufacture-finished-dosage-form-revision-1_en.pdf)

edition_specific_features.feature: Equipment status and electronic logbook tied to BMR steps (cleaning type, cleaned-by/checked-by, product and batch sequence, maintenance, calibration)
edition_specific_features.why: Chronological equipment logs are mandatory; linking them to the BMR removes duplicate entries and blocks use of unclean or uncalibrated equipment.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.67, 211.182 (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-211/subpart-J/section-211.182)

edition_specific_features.feature: Tablet IPC workstation: direct integration with multi-parameter testers (weight, thickness, diameter, hardness), friabilator and DT apparatus; configurable sampling frequency per MBR; due-timers; live SPC (X-bar/R, Cpk)
edition_specific_features.why: Compression IPC produces the most data in a tablet BMR. Automatic capture prevents backdating, and SPC supports 211.110(b) statistical in-process specifications.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110(a)-(b) (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-211/subpart-F/section-211.110); FDA draft 211.110 guidance Jan 2025 (https://www.fda.gov/media/184825/download)

edition_specific_features.feature: Automatic bracketing and segregation: when an IPC fails, the system marks every container and quantity produced since the last passing check as quarantined and opens a deviation
edition_specific_features.why: Prevents release of material produced during an excursion; the business logic has no gap.

edition_specific_features.feature: Versioned pharmacopoeial calculators (Ph.Eur. 2.9.5, USP <905> AV/WV, <1216>, <701> staging, <711> S1-S3, Ph.Eur. subdivision), bound to the pharmacopoeia edition effective on the test date
edition_specific_features.why: Different markets reference different pharmacopoeias (USP-NF, Ph.Eur. 12th/13th Ed., IP 2026). Automated pass/fail removes calculation errors. Note: USP <2091> must not be used for drug tablets.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: USP <905> Stage 4 official 1 Aug 2023; Ph.Eur. 13.1 implementation 1 Jan 2027 (https://www.edqm.eu/en/-/european-pharmacopoeia-issue-13.1-now-available); IP 2026 effective 1 Jul 2026 (https://www.ipc.gov.in/news-highlights/1416-registration-open-for-the-release-of-the-10th-edition-of-indian-pharmacopoeia-2026-ip-2026.html)

edition_specific_features.feature: Blend uniformity module: graphical sampling map per blender, thief/sample IDs, sample-size check (1-3× unit dose), LIMS result import, statistics and OOS workflow
edition_specific_features.why: BU sampling errors are common. Enforcing the validated map makes results defensible.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110(a)(3), 211.160(b); FDA CGMP Q&A production and process controls (https://www.fda.gov/drugs/guidances-drugs/questions-and-answers-current-good-manufacturing-practice-regulations-production-and-process); ISPE BUCU / ASTM E2709/E2810

edition_specific_features.feature: Punch and die (tooling) management: tooling master (shape, embossing, score) linked to the product, issue/return, pre/post inspection, cumulative compression counts, retirement limits
edition_specific_features.why: Wrong or damaged tooling causes mix-ups (wrong embossing) and defects; tooling identity is part of product identity.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.188(b)(2) (major equipment identity), 211.67; industry best practice

edition_specific_features.feature: Metal detector and vision-system challenge logs with interlocks (production cannot continue until the challenge is recorded), plus bracketing on failure
edition_specific_features.why: Ensures inspection systems work throughout the batch.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: Schedule M Part I-B (secondary-source text); 21 CFR 211.68; EU GMP Ch.5 (checks on electronic code readers, label counters)

edition_specific_features.feature: Coating module: weight-gain tracker, suspension quantity calculator, spray-parameter trend capture, suspension hold timer
edition_specific_features.why: Weight gain is the coating endpoint and a CQA surrogate for functional coats.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.110; Schedule M Part I-B (coating suspension made afresh)

edition_specific_features.feature: Stage-wise yield and reconciliation engine: limits from the MBR, automatic calculation, second-person verification, auto-deviation outside limits (both sides of 100%), release block until closed
edition_specific_features.why: Covers 211.103/211.186/211.192 without loopholes.

edition_specific_features.feature: Packaging material control: artwork-version validation against the packaging instruction and MA, count-by-weight calculator, specimen image capture of every printed component and on-line coding (camera snapshot)
edition_specific_features.why: Labelling mix-ups are a leading recall cause; specimens are required in the record.

edition_specific_features.feature: Digital line clearance: station-by-station checklists with photos, dual sign-off (performed/verified), blocking of the next step, previous-batch documents auto-closed
edition_specific_features.why: Line clearance must be documented in the batch record and done immediately before use.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.130(e); EU 4.20 pre-check, 4.18(f)-(g), Ch.5 packaging operations

edition_specific_features.feature: Label reconciliation with 211.125(c) waiver logic (only if a validated 100% electronic verification under 211.122(g)(2) is active and its challenges passed) and a destruction workflow with witness
edition_specific_features.why: Implements the regulatory exception exactly and no more broadly.
edition_specific_features.regulatory_basis: 21 CFR 211.125(c),(e), 211.122(g) (https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2012/03/20/2012-6502/current-good-manufacturing-practice-in-manufacturing-processing-packing-or-holding-of-drugs-revision)

edition_specific_features.feature: Blister leak-test module and bottle-line checks (count, desiccant, torque, induction seal) with bracketing on failure
edition_specific_features.why: Container-closure integrity is critical for moisture-sensitive tablets.

edition_specific_features.feature: Serialization integration (L3/L4 connectors): SN pool management, code grading capture, unit-to-case-to-pallet aggregation, SN reconciliation, market rule packs (EU FMD, DSCSA, India H2 Table 1 and Table 2 dates)

User's question (relayed): are graph-based data structures or databases a good idea for the eBMR? My view, which is a design judgment and not from a regulation: the regulated system of record (MBR versions, executed steps, e-signatures, audit trails, reconciliations) is transactional and needs ACID guarantees, immutable audit trails, validated backup/restore and Part 11/Annex 11 controls. A relational store is the conventional and easiest-to-validate choice. Several tablet-specific problems are graph-shaped, though: batch genealogy with split/merge (sub-lots → blend → cores → bulk → multiple packaging orders), serialization aggregation trees, recall/impact queries that must 'extend to other batches' (211.192), and master-recipe process flows as DAGs with variant branches. Recommended: model these as graphs (edge tables with recursive queries in the relational store, or a derived, read-only graph projection for where-used/recall analytics). Do not make a separate graph database the GxP system of record unless it is validated with equivalent audit-trail and data-integrity controls. Confirm with the architecture workstream.
